- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 79.16 → 80+ forecast), then undercorrects or lags in subsequent days.
- Underestimates in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days of 30d), suggesting mean reversion bias or delayed reaction to market signals.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than true price volatility, underreacting to short-term volatility spikes.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price increases — true price often rises faster than forecast suggests.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias, especially when history includes recent high prices (e.g., 79+), suggesting overconfidence in continuation.
- When history includes a recent low, model tends to underestimate the rebound, missing the “recovery” phase.
- Model fails to capture “reversal” patterns — e.g., after a spike, true price often dips slightly before resuming trend, but model holds high.
- Forecast tends to be “sticky” — resistant to downward corrections even when history shows weakening momentum.
- Model overweights recent history (last 5–10 days) in forecasting, leading to overreaction to short-term noise.
